topic: WR250F uncorking and the competition kit
statement: As delivered the 2015-generation WR250F is held back for sound and emissions and has a lean spot around one-third throttle that is annoying in technical riding. Closed-course uncorking is three parts: remove the throttle stop, the smallest muffler restrictor and the intake snorkel; it gains low and midrange and stays quiet. Yamaha's competition kit (about $110) is a replacement competition ECU supplied with a full-travel throttle stop screw; it removes the lean spot and works with the Power Tuner, which is sold separately. A YZ250FX ECU tried in testing removed the lean spot and added low and midrange, but the headlight did not work with it.

vals.uncork: throttle stop, small muffler restrictor, intake snorkel

notes: Test bike was a 2015; applied to the same generation through 2017.

topic: TX 300 2017 tester fork and shock settings
statement: A magazine crew's 2017 TX 300 setup for a rough motocross track. Fork (AER 48): 150 psi (stock 139), compression 15 clicks out (stock 12), rebound 6 out (stock 12), legs at the second line. Shock (42 N/mm spring): race sag 105 mm (the test listed stock as 110; the owner's manual gives 105), high-speed compression 1-1/2 turns out (stock 2), low-speed compression 10 out (stock 15), rebound 8 out (stock 15). Stock it is soft on big hits and the shock squats in corners.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2017 Husqvarna TX300 race test
